sources.cite: OpenSSF, Secure Coding Guide for Python, CWE-78: OS Command Injection
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. With shell=True 'an actual shell is invoked to run a line of commands'; building a command string from less-trusted data lets an attacker inject commands with separators such as ';'; prefer shell=False with an argument list, and Python modules such as pathlib or shutil where they exist; shell=False 'is not going to prevent all attacks' on its own.
Every organization, person, count and deadline is invented teaching data; tool output is an authored rendering in the tool style.

scoring.modelReasoning: A file name with ; and a pipe in it is harmless until a shell parses it. subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) with an f-string does exactly that, so the name's second half would run as a command. Pass an argument list with shell=False, so the name is a single argument, and add check=True, capture_output=True, text=True and a timeout. shlex.quote is the fallback only when a shell is unavoidable; stripping semicolons misses &&, | and $( ).
